description: Deterministic MAC well-formedness fixtures for the wire `v1` value (the §9.2 header MAC, mirrored by the §9.7 directive and §9.8 entry contexts). The shared rule — base64url alphabet, RFC 4648 padding tolerated only when structurally valid, decoded length ≥ 32 bytes, and NOTHING more (no canonical round-trip) — is exported by the reference as `isWellFormedMac`/`decodeMac` beside the signer that emits `v1`, so consumers import the rule instead of re-deriving it: a hand-rolled second validator with the wrong alphabet rejected 100% of conformant traffic (issue #41; oh-hai#711). Executed by the runner against the reference helpers themselves.
obligation: For each case, a consumer's well-formedness check MUST classify `value` as its `expect`, and its decoder MUST yield raw bytes for well-formed values (matching `decoded_length` where pinned, and byte-identical to `decodes_identically_to` where pinned) and nothing for ill-formed ones. Screening is exactly: alphabet `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`; optional trailing `=` padding accepted only in the exact RFC 4648 count — pad chars exactly (4 − unpadded_length mod 4) mod 4, so a 43-char value takes exactly one `=` and a 44-char value takes none; decoded length ≥ 32 bytes (a floor, not an exact match — HMAC-SHA256 is exactly 32, ed25519 is 64). Deliberately NOT enforced: canonical unpadded-form round-trip — a 43-char hex-shaped MAC is valid (the oh-hai#711 regression case). Deliberately rejected: the standard-base64 alphabet (`+`/`/`) that lenient decoders accept — a pinned tightening (issue #41); conformant §9.2 emitters are unaffected.
generator: The well-formed 43-char `v1` is real reference-signer output, never hand-computed: signResponse(buildSignedContext(signed_context), { key: test_key }) (reference/src/signing.ts) yields `canonical_jcs` and `v1`, which the runner re-derives as its drift control. The hex-shaped case is the first 43 chars of dp-001's payload_sha256; every reject is this vector's own `v1` minimally corrupted.

cases.note: fresh signer `v1` — 43 chars unpadded, the canonical §9.2 emission; decodes to exactly 32 bytes (HMAC-SHA256)
the same `v1` with exactly one `=` — 44 chars, structurally valid RFC 4648 padding: tolerated, and byte-identical to the unpadded form
43-char hex-shaped value (truncated SHA-256 hex) — every char is in the base64url alphabet and it decodes to 32 bytes; the oh-hai#711 regression case: no canonical round-trip check
standard-base64 `+` in place of `-` — §9.2 pins base64url; the deliberate tightening over Node's lenient decoder (issue #41)
standard-base64 `/` in place of `_` — same rule
43-char body + `==` — malformed padding: a 43-char value takes exactly ONE `=` (45 total ≢ 0 mod 4)
44-char unpadded-form body + a stray `=` — a body of length ≡ 0 mod 4 takes NO padding
decodes to 15 bytes — under the ≥ 32-byte floor (HMAC-SHA256 is exactly 32; ed25519 is 64 — floor, not exact)
